items.title: FCPE: A Fast Context-based Pitch Estimation Model
items.authors: Yuxin Luo(Fish Audio); Ruoyi Zhang(Fish Audio); Lu-Chuan Liu(University of Science and Technology of China); Tianyu Li(Fish Audio); Hangyu Liu(Fish Audio)
items.abstract: Pitch estimation (PE) in monophonic audio is crucial for MIDI transcription and singing voice conversion (SVC), but current deep learning methods often struggle to balance robust noise tolerance with computational efficiency. In this paper, we propose FCPE, a fast context-based pitch estimation model that employs a modified convolutional architecture with depth-wise separable convolutions to effectively capture mel spectrogram features while maintaining low computational cost and robust noise tolerance. Experiments show that our method achieves 96.79% Raw Pitch Accuracy (RPA) on the MIR-1K dataset, on par with the state-of-the-art methods. The Real-Time Factor (RTF) is 0.0062 on a single RTX 4090 GPU, which significantly outperforms existing algorithms in efficiency.

items.title: Audio-Visual Feature Reconstruction Pretraining for Noise-Robust Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Ivan Halim Parmonangan(Queensland University of Technology (QUT)); Tharindu Fernando(Queensland University of Technology (QUT)); Simon Denman(Queensland University of Technology (QUT))
items.abstract: Audiovisual emotion recognition fuses speech and facial expressions, yet real-world corruption such as background noise, reverberation, and dropped/frozen frames, can make the fusion fragile. A degraded input may dominate attention and suppress the clean input. Prior audiovisual pretraining solutions primarily optimize cross-modal alignment which can lose input details and often rely on Transformers, where the quadratic cost hinders long sequences. We propose a Mamba2 state-space fusion network with a self-supervised denoising pretraining stage, where clean features are reconstructed from corrupted audio-visual inputs only during pretraining to learn noise-robust representations. When applied to a downstream emotion recognition task, the proposed multimodal feature-reconstruction pretrained model delivers improvements under noisy audio and consistent gains over unimodal feature-reconstruction pretraining across diverse noisy/clean video settings, demonstrating improved robustness with efficient sequence modeling.

items.title: Smooth Formant Tracking with Differentiable Linear Prediction
items.authors: Bryn Luisi(Aalto University); Lauri Juvela(Aalto University)
items.abstract: Linear prediction methods for formant estimation are fast and interpretable, but assume local stationarity and Gaussian residuals. Hybrid neural methods are robust and accurate but lack interpretability and differentiability. We present LP-DDSP, a differentiable all-pole model that estimates formants by directly optimizing log-area ratios via a novel loss function that combines L1, L2, and temporal regularization terms. This approach addresses the limitations of classic LP by allowing for non-Gaussian residuals and smooth parameter tracks across frames. We also introduce SMELP, an end-to-end neural formant tracker that incorporates our differentiable LP loss, enabling joint learning of interpretable intermediate representations and formant predictions. Both methods achieve competitive performance relative to baselines: KARMA and Praat. Our methods enable fully differentiable, interpretable, and smooth formant tracking and can be extended to other speech processing tasks.

items.title: Automatic identification of the onset of creaky voice according to F0 instability
items.authors: Rasmus Puggaard-Rode(University of Oxford); Joshua Penney(Macquarie University)
items.abstract: Creaky voice serves a number of linguistic and extra-linguistic functions and is a commonly studied feature in phonetics. While methods are available for automatically evaluating whether creak is present within a window of speech, researchers who wish to identify transitions between creaky and modal portions of speech, and their precise temporal patterning, usually rely on manual annotation. In this paper, we propose a method for automatically identifying the onset of creak based on F0 instability, building on the common observation that creak is often accompanied by octave shifts. We evaluate the method by comparing automatically estimated with human-annotated creak onset from a previous study on creak as a cue to the coda voicing contrast in Australian English. The automatic method performs similarly to human annotators, and we show that our proposed automatic method and manual annotation yield similar results for the questions posed in the previous study.

items.title: Less is More: Boosting Bimodal Music Emotion Recognition with Adaptive Audio Sequence Compression
items.authors: Dinghao Zou(Wuhan University of Science and Technology)
items.abstract: Fusing audio and symbolic MIDI modalities delivers comprehensive affective cues for music emotion classification, yet audio features suffer from severe temporal redundancy compared with compact MIDI representations, leading to prominent information density imbalance that may hinder effective bimodal fusion. To address this, we exploit music's inherent temporal dynamics-preserving salient features in high-variation regions and averaging low-variation regions-we propose PoolingVQ. It leverages Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE) to quantize local audio features into index sequences indicating local variation intensity, which guides dynamic pooling (e.g., max pooling for high-variation segments) to filter redundancy while retaining emotional dynamics. Experiments on EMOPIA and VGMIDI show that audio sequence compression via PoolingVQ facilitates effective bimodal fusion, achieving state-of-the-art performance, thus offering a practical scheme for audio multimodal fusion.

items.title: Differentiable Pitch Matching with Auditory Models
items.authors: David Marttila(Queen Mary University of London); Joshua D. Reiss(Queen Mary University of London)
items.abstract: Differentiable Digital Signal Processing models for audio synthesis often rely on external fundamental frequency estimators, as common loss functions like Multi-Scale Spectral Loss (MSS) provide uninformative gradients for frequency-related parameters. While recent spectral-based losses offer improvements, they can fail on signals where perceived pitch does not correspond to a prominent spectral peak, like in the case of a missing fundamental. We propose a novel, perceptually-informed distance metric for pitch based on features from a differentiable computational auditory model. By processing auditory images to extract a timbre-normalized representation of periodicity, our metric is more robust to timbral variations. We evaluate our approach on a synthetic pitch-matching task and show that it can provide more informative gradients than Spectral Optimal Transport and MSS baselines. This work is a step towards allowing end-to-end training of DDSP models without external pitch estimators.

items.title: Layer-wise Probing of Whisper's Encoder Representations for Bengali Phone-like Units
items.authors: Munim Thahmid(BUET); Sadia Sharmin(BUET)
items.abstract: We investigate where Bengali phone-like units become linearly separable across the encoder layers of OpenAI's Whisper. Phone-like segments are obtained via MMS forced alignment on uromanized transcripts, and lightweight linear probes are trained per layer under speaker-disjoint evaluation. Whisper-small and Whisper-medium both peak in the mid-to-late layers, whereas Whisper-large-v3 forms a broad late-layer plateau with markedly less final-layer degradation. A self-supervised baseline (wav2vec2-XLSR) shows a far steeper late-layer decline, suggesting that supervised ASR training preserves phonetic detail deeper into the encoder. Per-class F1 analysis reveals that aspirated stops and affricates are separable from early layers, while nasals and sibilants drive mid-layer gains. We further validate these findings with ABX discriminability, alignment-confidence filtering, duration stratification, and an English MFA cross-lingual baseline.

items.title: Aligning MusicLLM with Emotion using Instruction Tuning and Feedback-Driven Alignment
items.authors: Takuya Hasumi(LY Corporation); Welly Naptali(LY Corporation)
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether music large language models (MusicLLMs) can be aligned for emotion regression. While MusicLLMs have shown strong performance in music information retrieval tasks, their ability to predict arousal and valence scores remains limited, since emotion regression has not been an explicit training objective. To examine whether MusicLLMs can be aligned with emotion, we train MusicLLMs on emotion regression and compare two strategies: instruction tuning and feedback-driven alignment. Our experiments show that task-aware instruction tuning enables MusicLLMs to predict emotion levels to some extent, although the accuracy remains limited. Applying feedback-driven alignment with a verifiable numerical reward substantially improves performance on both arousal and valence over instruction tuning alone. We further show that our approach improves emotion regression performance while maintaining MusicQA capability.

items.title: MultiLinguahah : A New Unsupervised Multilingual Acoustic Laughter Segmentation Method
items.authors: Sofia Callejas(Université Paris-Saclay; Universidad de Chile); Nahuel Gomez(Universidad de Chile); Catherine Pelachaud(Sorbonne University); Brian Ravenet(Université Paris-Saclay); Valentin Barriere(Universidad de Chile)
items.abstract: Laughter is a social non-vocalization that is universal across cultures and languages, and is crucial for human communication, including social bonding and communication signaling. However, detecting laughter in audio is a challenging task, and segmenting it is even more difficult. Currently, Machine Learning methods generally rely on costly manual annotation, and their datasets are mostly based on English contexts. Thus, we propose an unsupervised multilingual method that sets up the laughter segmentation task as an anomaly detection of energy-based segmented audio sequences. Our method applies an Isolation Forest on audio representations learned from BYOL-A encoder. We compare our method with several state-of-the-art laughter detection algorithms on four datasets, including stand-up comedy, sitcoms, and general short audio from AudioSet. Our results show that state-of-the-art methods are not optimized for multilingual contexts, while our method outperforms them in non-English settings.

items.title: Boundaryless Speech-to-Syllable Representations with Hierarchical CNN for Linguistically Inspired Automatic Stress Detection
items.authors: Namrata Mokshagundam(IIIT Hyderabad); Sai Harshitha Aluru(IIIT Hyderabad); Chiranjeevi Yarra(IIIT Hyderabad)
items.abstract: In stress-timed languages like English, word stress placement can change meaning, making automatic syllable stress detection vital for Computer Assisted Language Learning (CALL) systems, as L2 learners often misplace stress. Existing approaches rely on manually annotated boundaries or forced alignment, which require extensive labeling and suffer from alignment inaccuracies. We propose a fully boundary-independent framework using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for hierarchical time-compression, converting frame-level embeddings into compact syllable-level representations without explicit segmentation. To enforce the linguistic constraint that each word contains exactly one stressed syllable, we also incorporate a Post-net2.0 loss. Experiments on the ISLE corpus with German (GER) and Italian (ITA) learners show consistent improvements over boundary-dependent and prior boundary-independent SOTA models, achieving 94.86% (GER) and 96.24% (ITA), with gains up to 18.67% and 16.12%.

items.title: Instantaneous Pitch Estimation via Wave-U-Net-Based Fundamental Waveform Enhancement
items.authors: Junya Koguchi(CyberAgent); Tomoki Koriyama(CyberAgent)
items.abstract: Instantaneous pitch estimation plays an important role in analyzing steep pitch variations such as speech prosody and singing techniques. Conventional approaches estimate instantaneous frequency after isolating the fundamental waveform from signals that contain harmonics and noise, which makes the accuracy sensitive to imperfect fundamental filtering. In this study, we formulate fundamental waveform filtering as a speech enhancement problem. Specifically, we train a Wave-U-Net model to extract a fundamental waveform from an input speech signal. The instantaneous pitch is then obtained by computing the instantaneous frequency from the analytic signal of the estimated fundamental waveform. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms conventional deterministic approaches and provides accurate and robust instantaneous pitch estimation across diverse domains, including speech, singing voice, musical instruments, and degraded speech signals.

items.title: TF-MossFormer: Integrating Convolution Gated Local-Global Attentions for Enhanced Time-Frequency Domain Monaural Speech Separation
items.authors: Shengkui Zhao(Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group); Zexu Pan(Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group); Haoxu Wang(Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group); Biao Tian(Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group); Bin Ma(Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group); Xiangang Li(Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group, China)
items.abstract: Transformers with global attention capture long-range dependencies but can miss the fine-grained local continuity crucial for speech separation. We propose TF-MossFormer, a time-frequency transformer that combines local and global attention to jointly model short- and long-range contexts for monaural speech separation. At its core is a content-aware sliding-window attention mechanism that dynamically adapts receptive fields for stronger local interactions, avoiding the rigidity of static convolutions. Unlike time-domain chunk-based methods, TF-MossFormer leverages the 2D spectrogram to model structure along both time and frequency axes. Convolutional gating between attention layers further improves feature selection and information flow. TF-MossFormer achieves SI-SDRi of 22.6, 24.0, and 24.4 dB on WSJ0-2Mix with 5.9M, 16.9M, and 25.4M parameters, respectively, outperforming prior approaches.

items.title: Enroll-on-Wakeup: A First Comparative Study of Target Speech Extraction for Seamless Interaction in Real Noisy Human-Machine Dialogue Scenarios
items.authors: Yiming Yang(Shanghai Normal University); Guangyong Wang(Unisound AI Technology Co., Ltd.); Haixin Guan(Unisound AI Technology Co., Ltd. ); Yanhua Long(Shanghai Normal University)
items.abstract: Target speech extraction (TSE) typically relies on pre-recorded high-quality enrollment speech, which disrupts user experience and limits feasibility in spontaneous interaction. In this paper, we propose Enroll-on-Wakeup (EoW), a novel framework where the wake-word segment, captured naturally during human-machine interaction, is automatically utilized as the enrollment reference. This eliminates the need for pre-collected speech to enable a seamless experience. We perform the first systematic study of EoW-TSE, evaluating advanced discriminative and generative models under real diverse acoustic conditions. Given the short and noisy nature of wake-word segments, we investigate enrollment augmentation using LLM-based TTS. Results show that while current TSE models face performance degradation in EoW-TSE, TTS-based assistance significantly enhances the listening experience, though gaps remain in speech recognition accuracy.

items.title: HRTF-guided Binaural Target Speaker Extraction with Real-World Validation
items.authors: Yoav Ellinson(Bar-Ilan University); Sharon Gannot(Bar-Ilan University)
items.abstract: This paper presents a Head-Related Transfer Function (HRTF)-guided framework for binaural Target Speaker Extraction (TSE) from mixtures of concurrent sources. Unlike conventional TSE methods based on Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation or enrollment signals, which often distort perceived spatial location, the proposed approach leverages the listener's HRTF as an explicit spatial prior. The proposed framework is built upon a multi-channel deep blind source separation backbone, adapted to the binaural TSE setting. It is trained on measured HRTFs from a diverse population, enabling cross-listener generalization rather than subject-specific tuning. By conditioning the extraction on HRTF-derived spatial information, the method preserves binaural cues while enhancing speech quality and intelligibility. The performance of the proposed framework is validated through simulations and real recordings obtained from a head and torso simulator (HATS) simulator in a reverberant environment.

items.title: NeuroMultiSpEx: Neuro-Guided Target Speaker Extraction for Multi-Speaker Scenarios
items.authors: Dashanka De Silva(University of Bremen); Saurav Pahuja(University of Bremen); Siqi Cai(The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen; Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen); Tanja Schultz(University of Bremen); Haizhou Li(The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen)
items.abstract: Neuro-guided speaker extraction uses brain signals captured by EEG to extract attended speech from a multi-speaker mixture. Most studies address only 2-speaker scenarios. While real-world situations involve multiple concurrent talkers, multi-speaker neuro-guided extraction remains largely unexplored. We present NeuroMultiSpEx, a neuro-guided speaker extraction system for 4-speaker scenarios using mobile ear-EEG. Our approach integrates temporal synchronization cues from an EEG-based envelope encoder with speaker identity from an EEG-based speaker encoder through a gated fusion mechanism that adaptively weights "when" versus "who" guidance. Trained end-to-end, NeuroMultiSpEx demonstrates effective speaker extraction on an ear-EEG dataset and substantially outperforms competing systems across all evaluation criteria. To our knowledge, this is the first study on neuro-guided multi-speaker extraction using wearable ear-EEG, advancing toward practical brain-informed hearing aids.

items.title: USAD 2.0: Scaling Representation Distillation for Universal Audio Understanding
items.authors: Heng-Jui Chang(MIT); Alexander Liu(MIT); Saurabhchand Bhati(Amazon); Mrudula Athi(Amazon); Anton Ratnarajah(Amazon); Amit Chhetri(Amazon); James Glass(MIT)
items.abstract: Audio encoders are critical to modern audio applications as large language models (LLMs) increasingly rely on a single encoder for diverse inputs. While self-supervised learning (SSL) has yielded strong domain-specific encoders like speech or music experts, multi-domain approaches like USAD and SPEAR remain limited in coverage and evaluation. Recent studies also suggest supervised encoders align better with audio LLMs. We present USAD 2.0, a universal encoder integrating knowledge from both SSL and supervised foundation models. USAD 2.0 introduces domain-aware distillation to address teacher mismatch, extends coverage to the music domain, and adds second-stage supervised distillation for downstream use. We further scale the model to one billion parameters via depth scaling. Experiments show USAD 2.0 achieves strong or state-of-the-art performance across probing and LLM-based evaluations.

items.title: Latent Flow Matching Based Speech Separation Using Speaker Diarization
items.authors: Boris Rubenchik(Bar-Ilan University); Sharon Gannot(Faculty of Engineering, Bar-Ilan University, Israel); Ethan Fetaya(Faculty of Engineering, Bar-Ilan University, Israel)
items.abstract: This paper presents a novel generative approach to single-channel speech separation that integrates flow matching with end-to-end speaker diarization. Discriminative Deep Neural Networks (DNN)-based separation methods have demonstrated excellent performance in recent years. More recently, generative models have emerged as strong competitors for producing perceptually high-quality speech. We propose a framework that combines the representational strength of speaker diarization models with the high-fidelity generative capabilities of latent space Flow Matching. The method achieves high-quality separation while requiring training only of the latent generative U-Net component. In addition, we introduce a novel Adversarial Speaker Guidance (ASG) mechanism to mitigate speaker confusion. By conditioning on mixture-derived speaker attractors rather than traditional enrollment signals, the proposed approach improves intelligibility and reduces the occurrence of speaker confusion.

items.title: TGTSE: Token-Guided Target Speaker Extraction with Visual Cue
items.authors: Tongtao Ling(Southern University of Science and Technology); Shulin He(Southern University of Science and Technology); Zhong-Qiu Wang(Southern University of Science and Technology)
items.abstract: Utilizing visual cues for speaker extraction has demonstrated strong performance in noisy-reverberant environments. This paper proposes a token-guided paradigm for audio-visual target speaker extraction (AVTSE). Given a target speaker's lip movements in a facial video, the first goal is to extract coarse-grained semantic tokens associated with the lip movements. Second, we treat the predicted tokens as temporally aligned semantic cues to guide the speaker extraction system. We evaluate our approach on two benchmark datasets: VoxCeleb2-2Mix and LRS2-2Mix. Evaluation results demonstrate that our token-guided approach consistently outperforms conventional AVTSE systems.

items.title: Multi-View Based Audio Visual Target Speaker Extraction
items.authors: Peijun Yang(Wuhan University); Zhan Jin(Wuhan University); Juan Liu(Wuhan University); Ming Li(Wuhan University)
items.abstract: Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction (AVTSE) aims to separate a target speaker's voice from a mixed audio signal using the corresponding visual cues. While most existing AVTSE methods rely exclusively on frontal-view videos, this limitation restricts their robustness in real-world scenarios where nonfrontal views are prevalent. Such visual perspectives often contain complementary articulatory information that could enhance speech extraction. In this work, we propose Multi-View Tensor Fusion (MVTF), a novel framework that transforms multiview learning into single-view performance gains. During the training stage, we leverage synchronized multi-perspective lip videos to learn cross-view correlations through MVTF, where pairwise outer products explicitly model multiplicative interactions between different views of input lip embeddings. At the inference stage, the system supports both single-view and multi-view inputs. Experimental results show that in the singleview inputs, our framework leverages multi-view knowledge to achieve significant performance gains, while in the multi-view mode, it further improves overall performance and enhances the robustness. Our demo, code and data are available at ¹.

items.title: AV-SNINet: A multi-channel audio-visual speech-noise interaction network for Target Speaker Extraction with cross-beam attention
items.authors: Yanhui Tu(Anhui University); Runxiang Yu(iFlytek); Yi Fang(Chinese Academy of Sciences)
items.abstract: This paper proposes a multi-channel audio-visual speech-noise interaction network (AV-SNINet), which combines mask-based beamforming with a deep learning (DL) cross-beam attention mechanism. Unlike existing methods that mainly rely on lip-speech synchronization cues, the proposed cross-beam attention explicitly models frame-level interactions between target-beam and interference-beam features, enabling mutual-exclusion style suppression in the beam domain. In the first stage, an AV-DPCRN-guided GEVD beamformer uses spatial information to obtain target and interference beams. In the second stage, AV-SNINet jointly estimates speech and noise masks through a dual-branch interactive architecture. On our real-world recording dataset, AV-SNINet achieves a relative WER reduction of 28.23%, from 28.40% to 20.38% (AVG), over the first-stage baseline. On far-field LRS2 simulation, AV-SNINet achieves the best average WER of 17.20%.

items.title: MeloDISinger: Melody-Aware & Duration-Preserving Singing Voice Editing with Audio Infilling
items.authors: Yoonjeong Park(KAIST); Jaekwon Im(KAIST); Juhan Nam(KAIST)
items.abstract: Text-based singing voice editing (SVE) aims to revise sung lyrics while preserving the original melody, total duration, and non-edited regions. In this paper, we propose MeloDISinger, a flow-matching-based SVE model for melody-aware and duration-preserving editing. Its core module, MeloDRP, predicts fixed-budget duration ratios, enabling explicit span-wise duration control. For melody-aware duration allocation, MeloDRP fuses phonetic cues with pseudo-MIDI melodic context through cross-attention, while temporal-overlap supervision encourages soft phoneme-note correspondences. We further use a flow-matching mel decoder for audio infilling to synthesize edited regions while preserving surrounding context. In addition, we introduce a duration-aware edited-lyric generation pipeline using WhisperX and an LLM to construct feasible evaluation scenarios. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both objective and subjective evaluations.

items.title: SingFox: A Multi-Lingual Singfake Detection Corpus
items.authors: Arth J. Shah(DAU); Devanshi K. Trivedi(SCET); Himanshi U. Borad(SCET); Hemant A. Patil(DAU)
items.abstract: In this work, we introduce SingFox, a comprehensive and large-scale dataset specifically to support robust evaluation of singing deepfake detection, and source tracing systems. SingFox is divided into six distinct tracks (T1-T6), each targeting a unique form of novelty–ranging from language diversity (global and Indic), genre-specific music, and alternative fake generations. The dataset encompasses over 1,13,802 audio clips across 20 languages, totaling more than 126.32 hours of audio data, and 1150 variety of singers. Each track is designed to imitate real-life situations and see how reliably the model performs under different conditions and to check its robustness. SingFox aims to foster reproducibility and accelerate research in singing deepfake detection by proposing a reliable dataset for both singfake detection task, and source verification task (explainability of model). We obtained highest accuracy of 77.84 % while cross-testing models trained on various datasets.

items.title: Singing Voice Conversion via Shared Speaker Space and Min-Pooling Adversarially Enhanced Flow Matching
items.authors: Yuye Hu(Xinjiang University); Ayiduosi Tuohan(Xinjiang University); Tianqi Ning(Xinjiang University); CuiCui Zhu(Xinjiang University); Hao Huang(Xinjiang University; Xinjiang Key Laboratory of Multi-lingual Information Technology; Joint International Research Laboratory of Silk Road Multilingual Cognitive Computing)
items.abstract: Singing Voice Conversion (SVC) faces a trade-off between singer feature disentanglement and singing quality. To address this, this paper proposes the MinFlow-SVC framework, a conditional flow matching-based SVC method enhanced by min-pooling adversarial training. We adopt a KNN-based approach to map source singer features into a shared singer space, removing source timbre to obtain content features like pitch, phonetics and singing expression. To further enhance generation quality, we introduce a min-pooling adversarial training strategy, which can detect and correct KNN-induced feature inconsistencies and improve conditional flow matching generation quality with harmonic awareness. Experiments show our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art SVC baselines in naturalness, intelligibility, timbre similarity and singing stability.

items.title: YingMusic-Singer: Controllable Singing Voice Synthesis with Flexible Lyric Manipulation and Annotation-free Melody Guidance
items.authors: Chunbo Hao(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.; Giant Network); Junjie Zheng(Giant Network); Guobin Ma(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Yuepeng Jiang(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Huakang Chen(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Wenjie Tian(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Gongyu Chen(Giant Network); Zihao Chen(Giant Network); Lei Xie(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.)
items.abstract: Regenerating singing voices with altered lyrics while preserving melody consistency remains challenging, as existing methods either offer limited controllability or require laborious manual alignment. We propose YingMusic-Singer, a fully diffusion-based model enabling melody-controllable singing voice synthesis with flexible lyric manipulation. The model takes three inputs: an optional timbre reference, a melody-providing singing clip, and modified lyrics, without manual alignment. Trained with curriculum learning and Group Relative Policy Optimization, YingMusic-Singer achieves stronger melody preservation and lyric adherence than Vevo2, the most comparable baseline supporting melody control without manual alignment. We also introduce LyricEditBench, the first benchmark for melody-preserving lyric modification evaluation. The code, weights, benchmark, and demos are publicly available at https://github.com/ASLP-lab/YingMusic-Singer-Plus.

items.title: CTMusic: A Traditional Chinese Instrumental Music Dataset Towards Text-to-Music Generation
items.authors: Zixing Zhang(Hunan University); Yimin Cao(Hunan University); Haotian Guo(Hunan University); Bin Wang(Hunan University); Jing Han(Hunan University; Yuelushan Center for Industrial Innovation)
items.abstract: Text-to-music generation has recently achieved remarkable progress. However, existing studies predominantly focus on Western music, leaving the domain of traditional Chinese music underexplored. A primary reason for this gap is the scarcity of well-annotated text-music paired datasets. To bridge this gap, we introduce CTMusic, a traditional Chinese instrumental music dataset designed for text-to-music generation. CTMusic comprises 741 carefully annotated text-music pairs with over 42 hours of audio, covering a diverse range of traditional Chinese instruments in both solo and ensemble settings. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CTMusic by fine-tuning Stable Audio Open on it and further provide an improved model that better captures the unique characteristics of traditional Chinese music. To our knowledge, CTMusic is the first dataset of its kind and offers new possibilities for Chinese music generation. The dataset is publicly available at: https://frei-2.github.io/CTMusic.

items.title: SRF-SVB: Style-Consistent Singing Voice Beautifying via Rectified Flow
items.authors: Wenhui Li(Harbin Institute of Technology); Biao Dong(Harbin Institute of Technology); Liwei Hu(Harbin Institute of Technology); Jiqing Han(Harbin Institute of Technology); Yongjun He(Harbin Institute of Technology)
items.abstract: Singing voice beautifying (SVB) aims to correct pitch and rhythm of amateur singing while enhancing vocal quality, preserving lyrics and the singer's timbre. Existing methods, however, suffer from limited generation quality and efficiency, and tend to neglect the preservation of the singer's style. We propose SRF-SVB, a style-consistent model for SVB via rectified flow, which achieves high-fidelity and efficient beautification covering pitch and rhythm correction. Furthermore, we design a context-guided masked mel-spectrogram inpainting mechanism that effectively preserves the amateur singer's style, including unique timbre and expressive patterns. Experiments on both English and Chinese test sets show that SRF-SVB outperforms baseline models in most objective and subjective metrics.

items.title: Towards Unified Song Generation and Singing Voice Conversion with Accompaniment Co-Generation
items.authors: Ziyu Zhang(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Chunyu Qiang(Kuaishou Technology); Xiaopeng Wang(Beijing Institute of Technology); Yuxin Guo(Chinese Academy of Sciences); Kang Yin(Kuaishou Technology); Wenjie Tian(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Jingbin Hu(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Tianlun Zuo(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Zhao Guo(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Teng Ma(Kuaishou Technology); Yuzhe Liang(Kuaishou Technology); Chen Zhang(Kuaishou Technology); Lei Xie(Northwestern Polytechnical University)
items.abstract: While song generation and singing voice conversion (SVC) have evolved significantly, they have long been developed isolated: the former lacks zero-shot speaker cloning, while the latter overlooks vocal-accompaniment synergy. To bridge this gap, we propose UniSinger, the first end-to-end framework unifying speaker cloning song generation and accompaniment co-generation SVC. Building on the multimodal diffusion transformer, we construct a unified speaker embedding space transferring speaker representation from SVC to song generation, endowing fine-grained cross-task timbre control. To mitigate multi-task optimization conflicts, we design a curriculum learning strategy using task-specific modality masking to guide the model to gradually master the generative mechanisms among semantic content, vocal timbre, and accompaniment. Experiments show state-of-the-art performance on both tasks and realizes complementary benefits, offering new possibilities for intelligent music production.

items.title: Towards Chinese Yue Opera Singing Voice Synthesis: A Benchmark with Dataset, Data Augmentation and Baseline Model
items.authors: Peng Bai(Xiamen University; Alibaba Group); Chenyang Lyu(Alibaba Group); Yue Zhou(Xiamen University); Wujin Sun(Xiamen University); Longyue Wang(Alibaba Group); Weihua Luo(Alibaba Group); Xiaodong Shi(Xiamen University)
items.abstract: This paper establishes the first comprehensive benchmark for Singing Voice Synthesis (SVS) of Chinese Yue Opera in the Wu dialect, addressing a critical gap in this unexplored field. Our benchmark integrates three key components: (1) the Yue Opera Audio-Text (YOAT) dataset, a high-quality corpus of 565 studio recordings with phoneme-level alignments for duration and pitch; (2) targeted data augmentation methods from the perspectives of pronunciation and pitch; and (3) YueOpera-Singer, a strong baseline model built on conditional flow-matching. Comprehensive objective and subjective evaluations verify the reliability of the YOAT dataset and the effectiveness of the proposed data augmentation methods. YueOpera-Singer delivers competitive synthesis quality with a subjective MOS of 3.92, acting as a robust baseline for the benchmark. The dataset, code, and demo samples are publicly available on the https://anonymous.4open.science/api/repo/YueOpera_Benchmark-6914/file/index.html.

items.title: Back to Ear: Perceptually Driven High Fidelity Music Reconstruction
items.authors: Kangdi Wang(Chinese Academy of Sciences; Ear-lab; Initi-AI Ltd); Zhiyue Wu(Ear-lab); Rui Lin(Ear-lab); Junyu Dai(ear-lab); Tao Jiang(Initi-ai Ltd)
items.abstract: Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) are essential for large-scale audio tasks like diffusion-based generation. However, existing open-source models often neglect auditory perception, resulting in poor phase accuracy and stereo representation. We propose ear-VAE, an open-source music reconstruction model that optimizes the VAE training paradigm. Our contributions are threefold: (i) A K-weighting perceptual filter applied prior to loss calculation to align the objective with auditory perception. (ii) A phase-aware correlation loss improving stereo coherence and spatial consistency. (iii) A spectral supervision scheme where magnitude loss is applied to all MSLR components, while phase is supervised only on LR components. Experiments show ear-VAE substantially outperforms leading open-source models across diverse metrics, showing particular strength in reconstructing high-frequency harmonics and spatial characteristics.

title: Multilingual, Cross-lingual & Low-Resource ASR
header: Tuesday 29 September 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area 8 - Poster 1 - Multilingual, Cross-lingual & Low-Resource ASR

items.title: PART: Progressive Alignment Representation Training for Multilingual Speech-To-Text with LLMs
items.authors: Pei Zhang(Alibaba Group; University of Macau); Andong Chen(Alibaba Group); Xi Chen(Alibaba Group; Chinese University of Hong Kong (Shenzhen)); Baosong Yang(Alibaba Group); Derek F. Wong(University of Macau); Fei Huang(Alibaba Group)
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have expanded from text to speech, giving rise to Speech Large Models (SLMs). A key challenge is aligning speech and text representations, which becomes harder in multilingual settings. Existing methods often freeze LLM parameters and train the encoders on multilingual multi-task data, often collapsing language representations into an shared space and hurting performance. We introduce Progressive Alignment Representation Training (PART), a multi-stage and multi-task framework that performs fine-grained alignment across languages and diverse speech tasks. During training, we progressively unfreeze the SLMs parameters, while introducing different types of multilingual tasks stage by stage to enhance multilingual speech-text alignment. Experiments on multiple mainstream benchmarks show that PART surpasses conventional approaches, with analysis confirming its ability to balance language-specific distinctions for robust multilingual speech-text alignment.

items.title: Alignment-Aware Continued Pre-training for Multilingual Speech Representation Learning
items.authors: Xun Lu(CAS; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences); Xuyang Wang(CAS; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences); Fan Feng(CAS; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences); Gaofeng Cheng(CAS; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences); Pengyuan Zhang(CAS)
items.abstract: Large multilingual self-supervised learning (SSL) models provide strong acoustic representations; they are typically adapted to ASR through direct supervised fine-tuning. This paradigm defers acoustic–symbol alignment entirely to the fine-tuning stage, which may limit cross-lingual generalization under heterogeneous scripts and long-tailed language distributions. We propose an alignment-aware continued pre-training framework on top of multilingual SSL foundation models.Instead of direct fine-tuning, we introduce an intermediate stage that jointly optimizes SSL and CTC objectives to impose textual alignment constraints on representation learning. We analyze the ASR performance of different modeling units introduced in the alignment and introduce a language-aware dual-codebook quantizer to mitigate multilingual competition. Experiments demonstrate consistent gains over direct fine-tuning and continual SSL adaptation, with improved cross-lingual transfer under unified textual spaces.

items.title: Synthetic Audio Generation Framework for Air Traffic Control Speech Recognition
items.authors: Raphaël Bagat(CNRS; LORIA); Zhe Zhang(National Institute of Informatics); Junichi Yamagishi(National Institute of Informatics); Irina Illina(Université de Lorraine); Emmanuel Vincent(Inria)
items.abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems, despite achieving remarkable accuracy in general-purpose domains with native speech (L1), struggle in domains like Air Traffic Control (ATC) due to strong channel noise, a presence of non-native (L2) English accents, and data scarcity. We propose a synthetic data generation pipeline with acoustical properties simulations specifically designed to address this lack of real data to improve recognition accuracy in the ATC domain. Our approach leverages a combination of neural generation techniques, including Text-to-Speech, Voice Conversion, L2-to-L1 accent conversion, and a novel controllable L1-to-L2 accent conversion framework built to simulate accented speech. Our experiments with the Whisper model on the ATCO2 corpus demonstrate that fine-tuning with either synthetic data alone, or a mix of real and synthetic data, significantly improves the word error rate over out-of-the-box and real data only baselines respectively.

items.title: GigaAM Multilingual: Foundation Model for Underrepresented Languages
items.authors: Andrei Kuzmenko(SaluteDevices); Alexandr Maximenko(SaluteDevices); Aleksandr Kutsakov(SaluteDevices); Georgii Gospodinov(SaluteDevices); Dmitrii Bolotov(SaluteDevices); Oleg Kutuzov(SaluteDevices); Pavel Bogomolov(SaluteDevices); Fyodor Minkin(SaluteDevices)
items.abstract: Despite recent scaling successes, multilingual ASR performance remains highly uneven, with long-tail languages suffering from severe data scarcity. This work addresses the challenge of building robust foundation models for underrepresented Central Asian languages (Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Uzbek). We present GigaAM Multilingual, a Conformer encoder pre-trained on 2M hours of audio using a HuBERT-style objective. Crucially, we introduce a cluster-level data balancing strategy during pre-training and a domain-aware sampling method during fine-tuning to mitigate head-language dominance. In controlled comparisons, our approach outperforms strong open pre-trained encoders (Whisper Large v3, Omnilingual-1B) on target languages, achieving significant gains on spontaneous speech while maintaining efficiency. We release the foundation encoder and ASR model, offering a proven recipe for effective multilingual adaptation under realistic data imbalance.

items.title: Low-Resource Medical ASR for Rich Transcription in Latvian
items.authors: Arturs Znotins(University of Latvia); Normunds Gruzitis(University of Latvia); Andris Rozentals(Assistentis); Maris Golubovskis(DATI Group); Mikelis Gulbis(DATI Group); Roberts Dargis(Viroling Technology)
items.abstract: This paper investigates automatic speech recognition (ASR) for rich medical transcription in a low-resource setting. We compare end-to-end ASR models trained to produce formatted reports with a two-stage pipeline combining verbatim transcription and LLM-based post-editing. To address limited training data, we introduce an LLM-driven data curation approach that converts legacy verbatim transcripts into formatted data, and we augment training with LLM-corrected pseudo-labeled data. Our experiments, using 50 hours of manually transcribed medical dictation and an additional 75 hours of LLM-corrected pseudo-labeled audio, show that domain-adapted foundation models significantly improve transcription quality across word error rate, punctuation accuracy, and medical entity recognition. The results demonstrate that high-quality medical ASR with rich transcription is achievable for low-resource languages using limited domain data.

items.title: Probing LoRA-to-LoRA Cross-Lingual Transfer for Unseen Low-Resource Conditions in Whisper-Based ASR
items.authors: Hirak Mondal(Samsung R&D Institute); Spandan Dey(Samsung R&D Institute); Gopal Agrawal(Samsung R&D Institute)
items.abstract: Low-resource Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) remains a challenge despite large-scale pre-training, especially for languages with minimal representation. We investigate LoRA-to-LoRA transfer using Whisper, where a Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) module trained on a donor language, even one under-represented in the base model, initializes adaptation for a low-resource recipient. Unlike full fine-tuning, this approach preserves pretrained parameters, ensuring stable, parameter-efficient cross-lingual transfer. We propose a two-stage donor selection strategy that filters candidates by genealogical relatedness and identifies the optimal donor through orthographic-distributional similarity. Results demonstrate that donor-informed initialization consistently outperforms recipient-only adaptation, yielding relative Word Error Rate (WER) reductions of up to 17%. Our findings indicate that leveraging linguistically and orthographically aligned donors is critical for effective low-resource ASR.

items.title: Overcoming Decoder Inconsistencies in Whisper for Dravidian and Low-Resource Languages
items.authors: Chowdam Venkata Kumar(Media Analysis Group, Sony Research India); Kumud Tripathi(Media Analysis Group, Sony Research India); Pankaj Wasnik(Media Analysis Group, Sony Research India)
items.abstract: Multilingual ASR models such as Whisper perform well on high-resource languages but exhibit substantially higher Word Error Rates (WER) for Dravidian languages compared to Indo-Aryan ones. Through linguistic and dataset analysis, we show that Dravidian languages have longer words, higher vocabulary diversity, and lower repetition, resulting in sparse token distributions and frequent character-level substitution errors. Baseline fine-tuning further reveals decoder imbalance between self-attention (linguistic context) and cross-attention (acoustic cues). Although synthetic token-repetition experiments indicate potential gains, they are impractical. Motivated by these observations, we introduce two decoder-level enhancements: Weighted-Attention, which adaptively balances attention sources, and Self-Conditioning, which reinjects intermediate predictions to improve token consistency. Experiments demonstrate consistent WER reductions for low-resource and agglutinative languages.

items.title: The Impact of Informal Persian Speech on Low-Resource ASR and Speech Translation
items.authors: Hadi Alizadeh(Toorintan Company); Mohammad Asgari(Toorintan Company; IRIBU); Mohammad Sadegh Mehrabikia(Toorintan Company); Amir Koohnavard(Toorintan Company)
items.abstract: We investigate the impact of informal Persian speech on automatic speech recognition and speech translation in low-resource settings. Persian exhibits substantial variation between formal and informal registers, yet most publicly available datasets focus on formal speech, leaving informal variants underrepresented. To address this gap, we introduce the Toorintan-Persian Informal Dataset, a carefully transcribed and validated collection of informal speech from diverse speakers and contexts. We apply targeted normalization techniques to improve data consistency and fine-tune state-of-the-art models on this dataset. Experiments demonstrate that models trained on informal data generalize effectively across both formal and informal registers and outperform existing baselines in WER and BLEU scores. To facilitate further research, we also release a Persian text normalizer. Both the dataset and associated tools are publicly available on Hugging Face.

items.title: BELLA: Efficient Bilevel Learning with LoRA for Multilingual ASR
items.authors: A F M Saif(Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute); Xiaodong Cui(IBM); Brian Kingsbury(IBM); Tianyi Chen(Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute; Cornell Tech)
items.abstract: Multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) faces challenges due to diverse linguistic structures and resource disparities. We propose an efficient BilEvel Learning with LoRA for Multilingual Speech Recognition (BELLA), a framework that couples a pre-trained ASR encoder with a large language model (LLM) decoder via a trainable bridge to align speech representations with the LLM token space. The decoder incorporates mixture-of-experts LoRA (MoE-LoRA) modules for language specialization, guided by a router. Training is formulated as a bilevel program: the upper level optimizes router and expert LoRA modules for task performance, while the lower level updates the bridge and shared adapter for alignment. We develop an efficient single-loop, value-function-free penalty solver with practical updates. BELLA is parameter-efficient, scalable, and reduces cross-language interference. Experiments on five CoVoST 2 languages show consistent gains over strong multilingual ASR baselines.

items.title: Automatic Lyric Transcription for Greek Songs: Scaling and Task Composition Effects in Whisper Adaptation
items.authors: Maria Frangiadaki(Athena R.C.); Dimitrios Damianos(Athena R.C.); Kosmas Kritsis(Athena R.C.); Vassilis Katsouros(Athena R.C.)
items.abstract: Automatic Lyric Transcription (ALT) remains substantially more challenging than speech recognition due to melodic variability, rhythmic irregularity, and accompaniment interference. This is heightened in low-resource languages like Greek, where no prior benchmark for ALT exists. We present the first controlled study of Whisper adaptation for Greek ALT, investigating model scaling effects, task composition via multitask training in transcribe-translate ratios, and two-stage speech-to-singing adaptation. We also curate a segment-level aligned singing dataset based on the Greek Audio Dataset (GAD) using source separation and CTC forced alignment. Results show that scaling consistently improves performance, while multitask learning acts as a beneficial regularizer primarily for smaller-capacity models. The 2-stage adaptation in Whisper Large-v3 achieves a Word Error Rate (WER) of 27.2%, a significant improvement over zero-shot baselines, establishing the first Greek ALT benchmark.

items.title: CrossPhon-Tonal: Streamlining Cross-language Modeling for Forced Alignment in Low-resource Tonal Languages
items.authors: Hongchen Wu(Georgia Institute of Technology); Yixin Gu(University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)
items.abstract: Forced alignment is essential for speech research, yet most tonal languages lack language-specific acoustic models for automation and require intensive human labor. While cross-language modeling offers a solution by leveraging foreign acoustic models, it typically overlooks lexical tone (e.g., using English for Tibetan) or relies on scarce phonetic expertise to craft manual mappings (e.g., using Mandarin for Tibetan). CrossPhon-Tonal introduces a novel tone encoding that integrates automated tone mappings into the cross-language modeling pipeline. Tested on six typologically diverse tonal languages, CrossPhon-Tonal presents performance comparable to human expert-generated mappings in cross-language modeling for forced alignment in tonal languages, and matches or outperforms the performance of the state-of-the-art Global English model. This work provides a scalable, automated solution for forced alignment in under-resourced tonal languages without requiring manual phonetic intervention.

items.title: Learning Contextualized Tonal Contours from F0: A Core-Auxiliary Branched Transformer for Mandarin Tone Recognition
items.authors: Yi-Fen Liu(Feng Chia University); Xiang-Li Lu(Feng Chia University); Po-Yu Chiu(Feng Chia University)
items.abstract: This study proposes a Transformer-based framework for Mandarin tone recognition that relies solely on suprasegmental F0 information. A core-auxiliary branched architecture is introduced, where the core contour encoder (C-Net) learns contextualized tonal representations while detachable auxiliary branches provide additional gradient pathways through cross-attention and layer-specific attention pooling during training. By encoding structured F0 embeddings across syllable, word, and chunk granularities and modeling rhythmic variability with a rhythm encoder (R-Net), the proposed approach consistently outperforms a single-branch baseline, even when the auxiliary branches are removed during inference, thereby further improving computational efficiency.

items.title: ProWhistress: An Enhanced Dual-Stream Transcription Architecture for Prosody-Aware Sentence Stress Detection
items.authors: Hujian Gu(Southwest University); Li Tao(Southwest University); Fei Jiang(Chongqing Academy of Science and Technology); Ying Wang(Southwest University); Jingwei Qu(Southwest University); Zhaofang Yang(Southwest University)
items.abstract: Sentence stress is crucial for conveying speaker intent and meaning. Yet recent alignment-free stress detection models struggle to capture fine-grained prosody due to dominant semantic representations. In this work, we introduce ProWhistress, an enhanced dual-stream transcription architecture that integrates explicit acoustic modeling to effectively preserve fine-grained acoustic details and significantly improve stress detection robustness. To mitigate the scarcity of Mandarin sentence stress data, we introduce a customized data generation pipeline specifically tailored for Mandarin, yielding the 12-hour synthetic SinoStress-Syn and the 3-hour human-recorded SinoStress-Real benchmark. Evaluations across five English and Mandarin datasets show that ProWhistress significantly surpasses competitive baselines, demonstrating superior accuracy and impressive zero-shot generalization on real-world speech. Code page: https://github.com/Guhujian/ProWhistress.git.

items.title: A Novel Sentence Stress Detection Framework Leveraging Auxiliary Word-Stress Modeling and Loss Optimization
items.authors: Tien-Hong Lo(National Taiwan Normal University); Fong-Chun Tsai(National Taiwan Normal University); Ting-An Hung(National Taiwan Normal University); Yu-Hsuan Hsieh(National Taiwan Normal University); Yao-Ting Sung(National Taiwan Normal University); Berlin Chen(National Taiwan Normal University, Taiwan)
items.abstract: Prosodic stress is a crucial aspect of automatic pronunciation assessment (APA), encompassing both sentence stress detection (SSD) and word stress detection (WSD). SSD highlights semantically salient words that shape discourse meaning, while WSD identifies the primary stressed syllable within each word to ensure lexical clarity. However, most prior work treats SSD and WSD as independent tasks, overlooking their shared reliance on prosodic cues such as pitch, duration, and intensity. To address this gap, we propose an effective SSD approach combining SSD with auxiliary WSD via a novel modeling paradigm. In addition, we introduce a word-span stress regularizer (WSR) that concentrates token-level SSD probabilities within each stressed word span. Experiments on the TinyStress-15K benchmark show that the proposed method outperforms strong baselines, with the complete configuration achieving the best SSD result.

items.title: WhiSSDapt: Adaptive Fusion of Whisper Layer Embeddings for Sentence Stress Detection
items.authors: Someshwaran Murugaiyan(Vellore Institute of Technology); Jhansi Mallela(IIIT Hyderabad); Chiranjeevi Yarra(IIIT Hyderabad)
items.abstract: Sentence stress refers to the relative prominence of certain words within a sentence. Automatic sentence stress detection aims to identify these prominent words from spoken utterances and is important for effective Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) systems. Since sentence stress is context-dependent and relative in nature, modeling sequential dependencies across words is essential. Existing approaches use fixed-layer representations from large-scale pre-trained models like Whisper for detection. However, we observe that directly using representations from a single layer does not optimally capture prosodic cues, as different layers encode different levels of acoustic and contextual information. We propose a weighted layer fusion framework within Whisper that learns an optimal combination of encoder and decoder representations. Experiments on naturally spoken and synthetic datasets show an improvement of up to 4.48% and 6.09%, respectively, for sentence stress detection.

items.title: PhonLLM: Joint Phone Recognition and Phonological Process Inference for Child Speech
items.authors: Ilja Baumann(Technische Hochschule Nürnberg); Korbinian Riedhammer(Technische Hochschule Nürnberg); Tobias Bocklet(Technische Hochschule Nürnberg)
items.abstract: We introduce phonological process inference, a structured prediction task that explains deviations in child speech by jointly recovering canonical phone sequences and phonological process tags. The initial stage pretrains on phone recognition without text conditioning. In the second stage, we fuse embeddings of an expected phone sequence with downsampled audio tokens and train a single decoder to output canonical phones with explicit process tags. A rule-based augmentation pipeline injects process supervision at scale without manual labeling and supports multilingual training by swapping language-specific grapheme-to-phone (G2P) mappings. Experiments across multilingual child and clinical corpora show that joint modeling improves tagging accuracy and reduces phone error rates compared to ASR-based baselines, while producing interpretable phone-level diagnostics suitable for screening and Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Training (CAPT).

items.title: SignMatch: Aligning Pose Latent Diffusion via Multi-dimensional Rewards for Sign Language Video Generation
items.authors: Rongjie Huang(CUHK); Weidong Chen(CUHK); Helen Meng(CUHK); Xixin Wu(CUHK)
items.abstract: Sign language video generation (SLVG) aims to synthesize photo-realistic signing videos from spoken-language text while preserving signer identity and visual style, but remains challenging due to weak alignment between text semantics and fine-grained spatio-temporal motion. We present SIGNMATCH, a unified framework that couples an LLM-empowered pose-latent diffusion planner with a motion-aware sign video diffusion renderer conditioned on predicted motion latents and a reference image. To better align motion planning with downstream objectives, we apply Flow-GRPO post-training with semantic and visual rewards to optimize the pose-latent generator without updating the video renderer. Experiments on RWTH-2014T and How2Sign demonstrate consistent gains in translation-based semantic metrics and perceptual video quality, improving overall faithfulness and realism.

items.title: Building Tailored Speech Recognizers for Japanese Speaking Assessment
items.authors: Yotaro Kubo(Sakana AI); Richard Sproat(Sakana AI); Chihiro Taguchi(Sakana AI); Llion Jones(Sakana AI)
items.abstract: This paper presents methods for building speech recognizers tailored for Japanese speaking assessment tasks. Specifically, we build a speech recognizer that outputs phonemic labels with accent markers. Although Japanese is resource-rich, there is only a small amount of data for training models to produce accurate phonemic transcriptions that include accent marks. We propose two methods to mitigate data sparsity. First, a multitask training scheme introduces auxiliary loss functions including one that focuses on the pitch patterns. The second fuses two estimators, one over phonetic alphabet strings, and the other over text token sequences. We show that this approach is advantageous compared to the use of generic multilingual recognizers. The relative advantages of the proposed methods were also compared. Our proposed methods reduced the average of mora-label error rates from 12.3% to 7.1% over the CSJ core evaluation sets.

title: Speech and Language Technologies in Healthcare

items.title: TriageSim: A Conversational Emergency Triage Simulation Framework from Structured Electronic Health Records
items.authors: Dipankar Srirag(University of New South Wales); Quoc Dung Nguyen(University of New South Wales); Aditya Joshi(University of New South Wales); Padmanesan Narasimhan(University of New South Wales); Salil Kanhere(University of New South Wales, Sydney, Australia)
items.abstract: Research in emergency triage is restricted to structured electronic health records (EHR) due to regulatory constraints on nurse-patient interactions. We introduce TriageSim, a simulation framework for generating persona-conditioned triage conversations from structured records. TriageSim enables multi-turn nurse-patient interactions with explicit control over disfluency and decision behaviour, producing a corpus of ~800 synthetic transcripts and corresponding audio. We use a combination of automated analysis for linguistic, behavioural and acoustic fidelity alongside manual evaluation for medical fidelity using a random subset of 50 conversations. The utility of the generated corpus is examined via conversational triage classification. We observe modest agreement for acuity levels across three modalities: generated synthetic text, ASR transcripts, and direct audio inputs. We provide the code for TriageSim at https://github.com/dipankarsrirag/triage-sim.git.

items.title: DIALOG DeID: Role and Privacy Aware Transcription for Clinical Interviews Beyond WER
items.authors: Guilherme C. Oliveira(Monash University); Dominic Dwyer(University of Melbourne); Stephanie Fong(Monash University); Leandro A. Passos(São Paulo State University); Dan Mo(Monash University); Benjamin Dixon(Emory University); Phillip Wolff(Emory University); Scott W. Woods(Yale University); Martha Shenton(Harvard Medical School); Barnaby Nelson(University of Melbourne); Zongyuan Ge(Monash University)
items.abstract: Clinical risk interviews depend on who said what and on meaning-critical cues such as negation, modality/uncertainty, and time. We present DIALOG-DeID, a configurable pipeline for long-form clinical dialogue that integrates ASR, diarization, automatic role mapping (clinician vs. interviewee), and transcript de-identification within a unified segment representation. We propose an evaluation recipe beyond WER by combining (i) speaker-attributed WER (sWER) to capture misattribution, and (ii) Qualifier/Temporal Preservation (QTP-F1), an auditable lexical cue metric targeting negation, modality/uncertainty, and temporal anchors. On PSYCHS-Bench, the best aggregate WER was 13.3±1.4 while role-attributed sWER remained 33.1±6.7; semantic audit found cue drops in 20-24% of snippets and hard negation flips in 2-4%, motivating meaning-aware evaluation for privacy-constrained clinical ASR. Code: https://github.com/GuiCamargoX/dialog-deid.

items.title: Revisiting Emotion-Based Triage: Evidence from French Emergency Call Data
items.authors: Elio Stasica(Université de Lorraine); Clément Joly(Université de Lorraine); Amandine Lecomte(Université de Lorraine); Vincent P. Martin(Université de Lorraine); Romain Serizel(Université de Lorraine); Emmanuel Vincent(Université de Lorraine); Tahar Chouihed(Université de Lorraine)
items.abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) has been broadly studied to assist automatic triage in Emergency Call Centers (ECC), based on the assumption that emotion reflects medical urgency. However, this has not been tested on real data using clinically grounded priority labels. Using 250 calls of a French ECC annotated in 4 priority levels by dispatchers and metadata (age, sex, speaker role), we compare a categorical SER (discrete emotions) and a dimensional SER (arousal, valence), integrating the outputs into ordinal logistic regression models. Results show that categorical emotions do not improve prediction once metadata are included. Dimensional emotions show significant interactions between arousal, valence, and speaker role, but effects are speaker-dependent. Overall, metadata outperform emotion, provide stronger predictive power than emotion, questioning the utility of emotion-only approaches for emergency triage.

items.title: Surgical-Robot Command Spotting: Safety-Aware Learning for Compositional Commands
items.authors: Jaewon Lee(ETRI); Sang-Beom Lee(ETRI); Bum-Hwi Kim(ETRI); Kwang-Yong Kim(ETRI)
items.abstract: Voice control of a surgical-assistant robot must map short utterances to structured actions in the presence of surgical masks and operating-room (OR) noise, where misrecognition can result in unsafe motions. Each utterance in this task specifies either a movement direction with a discrete step magnitude (1–5) or a functional command. Treating each composed command as an independent class disregards this compositional structure. We propose a lightweight command-spotting model that factorizes commands into direction, mode, and magnitude. This model uses head-wise temporal attention pooling on a shared encoder and learns step magnitude via ordinal regression with per-sample loss masking and a training-only auxiliary head. On a Korean OR-command dataset evaluated using leave-one-speaker-out under clean/noise and mask/no mask conditions, our model achieves 95.36% joint command success, with a MAE of 0.0338 steps and a catastrophic step error rate of 0.60% (|Δ|≥3) on step commands.

items.title: Formant-Guided Speech Repair for Enhanced Comprehension of Dysarthric Speech
items.authors: Xin-Yu Chen(National Tsing Hua University); Jing-Tong Tzeng(National Tsing Hua University); Carlos Busso(Carnegie Mellon University); Chi-Chun Lee(National Tsing Hua University)
items.abstract: Dysarthria severely degrades speech intelligibility, limiting effective communication and social participation. While neural reconstruction shows promise, most methods operate as black boxes that overlook known acoustic patterns, e.g., vowel formants that are fundamental to human speech perception. We propose a modular framework featuring a formant-aligned spectral transformation (FAST) module. Unlike implicit approaches, FAST explicitly regularizes the acoustic space by correcting distorted formants prior to synthesis. Integrated with dysarthria-adapted ASR and speaker-adaptive TTS, our system enhances intelligibility while preserving identity and prosody. Experiments on Mandarin and English datasets demonstrate strong generalization. On the primary corpus, the framework achieves a 72.4% relative reduction in CER. Subjective evaluations further indicate over 90% gains in intelligibility, comprehension, and fluency, with listening effort reduced by 60.9%.

items.title: Stuttering Classification and Segmentation with Attention-Based Multiple Instance Learning
items.authors: Petar Sušac(University of Zagreb); Sebastian P. Bayerl(Rosenheim Technical University of Applied Sciences); Hrvoje Džapo(University of Zagreb)
items.abstract: Stuttering detection and classification using deep learning methods has the potential to improve the process of stuttering severity assessment. Most stuttering classification datasets provide clip-level labels, making them unsuitable for fine-grained frame-level classification needed to determine the duration of individual stuttering dysfluencies. To overcome this challenge, we present a multiple instance neural network architecture based on fine-tuned wav2vec 2.0, WavLM and Whisper encoders. We apply instance- and embedding-based multiple instance learning approaches to train models on a clip-level dataset for both clip-level and frame-level stuttering classification tasks. Our results show a 23% improvement in frame-level F1 score and between 2% and 9% in clip-level F1 score, demonstrating the ability of our models to utilize clip-level data for frame-level segmentation.

items.title: Evaluating Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Stuttering Detection Based on Self-Attention Weights of Temporal Acoustic Vector Sequence
items.authors: Genzo Miyahara(Doshisha University); Tsuneo Kato(Doshisha University); Akihiro Tamura(Doshisha University)
items.abstract: Stuttering event detection (SED) is expected to quantify frequencies with types of stuttering to support speech therapy. Various stuttering symptoms are categorized into five common disfluency types, but some types exhibit large acoustic variation across individuals and languages. Recent advances in SED have been driven by the growth of stuttering speech corpora, but SED research remains challenging for no- or low-resource languages. We focus on the "self-attention weights of temporal acoustic vector sequence" (SAWF) as a feature for language transferable SED. SAWF is considered robust to linguistic differences as it extracts repetitions and prolongations of similar acoustic properties. Experimental results of zero-shot cross-lingual evaluation using stuttering speech corpora in three languages showed F1 scores reaching 77-98% of those in a monolingual setting. Moreover, SAWF-based SED achieved comparable performance to a state-of-the-art model for language-dependent disfluency types.

items.title: Phoneme Error and Uncertainty Features for Interpretable Dysarthric Speech Assessment
items.authors: Zihan Zhong(University of Auckland); Qianli Wang(University of Auckland); Satwinder Singh(University of Auckland); Clarion Mendes(University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Mark Hasegawa-Johnson(University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Waleed Abdulla(University of Auckland); Seyed Reza Shahamiri(University of Auckland)
items.abstract: Prior work on phoneme-level dysarthric speech assessment has been limited to alignment-based methods and speaker-level intelligibility prediction. Here, we move to utterance-level, multidimensional assessment, investigating posterior-uncertainty features from a frozen connectionist temporal classification (CTC) phoneme recognizer as proxies for articulatory distortion. We combine them with phoneme error rates to form the Phoneme Error Decomposition (PED) feature family. PED is evaluated via logistic regression probing on the Speech Accessibility Project dataset with utterance-level expert ratings. We find that uncertainty-based features provide the strongest individual assessment signals. The full PED family achieves a mean Area Under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.80 on four primary dimensions, comparable to the performance of a strong SSL baseline (AUROC of 0.81). We further present a transparent, human-inspectable decision-tree pipeline based on PED, with a mean AUROC of 0.78.

items.title: Decoding while Adapting: Zero-Shot Online Speaker Adaptation via Audio-Textual Prompts for Elderly Speech Recognition
items.authors: Chengxi Deng(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Xurong Xie(Chinese Academy of Sciences); Shujie Hu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Mengzhe Geng(National Research Council Canada); Tianzi Wang(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Youjun Chen(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Huimeng Wang(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Haoning Xu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Jiajun Deng(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Xunying Liu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel cross-utterance audio-textual prompts based speaker adaptation approach for elderly speech recognition. It enables zero-shot, real-time adaptation to unseen speakers. Speech and text embeddings are extracted from the current and a few preceding utterances, before being fused in a cross-modal manner to produce compact speaker prompts that are more consistent than i/x-vectors and ECAPA-TDNN features. Experiments on the English DementiaBank Pitt and Cantonese JCCOCC MoCA elderly speech datasets suggest that the proposed online adaptation outperforms the speaker-independent (SI) model by statistically significant word error rate (WER) or character error rate (CER) reductions of 0.61% and 1.22% absolute (2.99% and 4.48% relative). Real-time factor (RTF) speed-up ratios of up to 9.83 times are obtained over offline batch-mode adaptation.
